name: PGC 28887 (Hubble)
blurb: PGC 28887, a slowly rotating early-type galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: pgc028887-hubble
story: At the heart of PGC 28887 lies a kinematically distinct core, a central knot of stars turning differently from the rest of the galaxy. Hubble's sharp view found no flattened core of light there, a hint that gas helped build it.

claims.text: PGC 28887 is one of the 12 slowly rotating early-type galaxies (ATLAS3D slow rotators) imaged by HST program GO-13324
PGC 028887 was targeted as a low angular momentum early-type galaxy

Hubble imaging showed the 12 newly imaged slow rotators, including PGC 28887, have core-less central light profiles, consistent with formation through accretion of counter-rotating gas or gas-rich mergers
PGC 028887 has a kinematically distinct core (an abrupt change in kinematic position angle)
